data.title: Bitcoin Drops Ahead of Clarity Act Vote. Why Cathie Wood's Dumping Crypto Stocks. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Callum Keown

It's crunch time for cryptocurrencies.

The Senate will vote on the Clarity Act, a key bill for crypto regulation, on Tuesday afternoon.

Bitcoin and crypto-exposed stocks were falling ahead of the vote, though, after enjoying a rally in recent months as the legislation's chances of being passed have come back from the dead.

It's still a tight call. GOP senators have been making an 11th-hour push to get support from Democrats, Barron's reported Monday. But the odds of the bill passing this year slipped to 19% Tuesday from 31% yesterday, according to prediction market Polymarket. Polymarket has a data sharing partnership with Dow Jones, the publisher of Barron's.

That move, and broader pre-vote nerves are being reflected in crypto markets. Bitcoin fell to $76,890 early in the day, down 1.6% over the past 24 hours, according to CoinDesk data. The world's largest cryptocurrency is up 31% since the start of July but remains 12% down in 2026.

Ethereum, the second largest crypto, slipped 1.9% to $2,475, while popular altcoin XRP edged 0.2% lower to $1.40.

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest took the opportunity to sell crypto-related stocks Monday, according to a trading notification. ARK's funds sold shares in CoinDesk owner Bullish, crypto exchange Coinbase, stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group, and Ethereum treasury company Bitmine Immersion Technologies.

Coinbase stock was down 3.9% in premarket trading, after rallying 9% in the previous session. Strategy, the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, was down 3.8% after a 4.6% rise Monday.

Write to Callum Keown at callum.keown@dowjones.com

data.title: Palm oil gains for second straight session on crude prices
data.description:
By Dewi Kurniawati

Malaysian palm oil futures gained for a second straight session on Tuesday, following crude oil prices that continued to climb.

The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange was up 33 ringgit, or 0.68%, at 4,883 ringgit ($1,196.08) a metric ton at close.

Malaysia's financial markets will be closed on Wednesday for a public holiday. Trading will resume on Thursday, September 17.

"BMD CPO futures were seen trading higher today following gains in energy prices," said Anilkumar Bagani, research head at the Mumbai-based vegetable oil broker Sunvin Group.

He added that additional support came from expectations of tightness next year due to Indonesia's B50 biodiesel mandate and a potential production reduction due to El Niño.

Oil prices rose more than 2% on Tuesday after attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure left the kingdom's East-West pipeline offline, raising fears that damage to energy infrastructure and transport routes could take longer to repair.

Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.

Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) dropped 1.07%, while its palm oil contract shed 0.46%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were up 0.58%.

Palm oil tracks rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

Malaysia has raised its October crude palm oil reference price to a level that maintains the export duty at 10%, a circular on the Malaysian Palm Oil Board website showed on Tuesday.

Cargo surveyors estimated that exports of Malaysian palm oil products for September 1 to 15 fell between 17.8% and 25.6% from a month earlier.

India's palm oil imports in August rose 7% from July to 782,761 metric tons, the Solvent Extractors' Association of India (SEA) said on Tuesday.

The ringgit , palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.21% against the dollar, making the commodity cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.

($1 = 4.0825 ringgit)

data.title: "The house" visits the House
data.description:
By Mike Dolan

The nervous start to the week for world markets has seen 10-year U.S. Treasury yields top 5% to hit their highest in 19 years, just as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent prepares to address Congress and the Federal Reserve starts its critical two-day meeting today.

The prospect of interest rate rises along with climbing energy prices remain the primary aggravators of government bonds, which sold off across the world overnight, with Japanese 10-year yields rising back above 3%.

Intense fighting in the Middle East saw Brent crude push above $107 per barrel once more on Tuesday, after prices briefly retreated on Monday following President Trump's suggestion of a Russia-Ukraine agreement to spare energy infrastructure in their war.

Bessent's appearance in front of the House Financial Services Committee later today will likely deal with a host of thorny issues: his seemingly failed attempt at capping Treasury yields, his joint intervention with Japan to lift the yen, the economic war with Iran and the president's promise to give Americans $5,000 checks in a total $1.3 trillion cash injection.

Bessent's view on what markets expect will be a quarter-point Fed rate hike on Wednesday will also grab headlines, with U.S. bond markets now attempting to price up to four rate rises over the next year.

Elsewhere, the doomsday AI narratives and calls for a slowdown in AI development spilled into chip stocks on Monday, with the SOX semiconductor index falling more than 5% for the first time since July, dragging the overall S&P 500 and Nasdaq into the red.

Trump rejected calls for more restrictions, claiming guardrails on AI were already sufficient.

Elsewhere, a sweep of Chinese economic numbers was a mixed bag, with industry numbers beating forecasts in August, but retail sales missing and house prices still declining.

Coming into Tuesday's open, world stocks and Wall Street futures are in the red.

Chart of the day

The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield, the benchmark long-term borrowing rate for the government and wider economy, topped 5% this week to hit its highest since the eve of the global banking crash in 2007.

Rising oil prices and widespread expectations of the first Fed interest rate rise in three years tomorrow are driving yields higher, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's recent attempts to calm the market via a series of small buybacks have failed to cap yields.

Bessent will speak to the House Financial Services Committee in Congress on Tuesday.

Today's events to watch

  • Fed's two-day policy meeting begins

  • U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent appears before Congress (10 a.m. EDT)

  • U.S. 20-year bond auction (1 p.m. EDT), New York Fed manufacturing survey for September (8:30 a.m. EDT)

Before you go, check out my latest column on why AI may be too big to slow.

And listen to the latest episode of the Morning Bid daily podcast, where we discuss everything on Scott Bessent's plate as he heads to the Hill later today.

data.title: ZAWYA: Globant, Aldar Properties induct AI-powered agents
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Globant, a digitally native company that helps organisations thrive in a digital and AI-powered future, has deployed an agentic AI solution for Aldar Properties, Abu Dhabi's largest real estate developer.

Built on Salesforce Agentforce and powered by Data 360, the initiative marks a significant step in how Mena's property sector is moving from AI experimentation to enterprise-scale deployment, with AI agents supporting customer engagement around the clock.

Mena is experiencing a structural overhaul of how cities are built and operated. According to private studies, the GCC PropTech sector is expanding at a 15.7% CAGR toward a projected value of $5.87 billion by 2032, while the broader Mena real estate market is forecast to grow 89% between 2026 and 2034. Saudi Arabia alone recorded SR1.2 trillion ($320 billion) in property transactions within a single 24-month window, as reported by the Saudi Real Estate Authority.

Conversational interface

Embedded directly into "Hello Aldar," Aldar's 24/7 AI-powered digital concierge and customer self-service platform, the solution gives homeowners a conversational interface to access property information, raise service requests, and track construction progress at any hour. Built as an extension of the existing LiveAldar experience, Hello Aldar ensures full consistency with backend processes and workflows already running on Salesforce. Within this platform, Agentforce solutions tackle the most friction-heavy moments in the homeowner journey: construction transparency and post-sale service.

The Construction Progress Agent translates technical construction data into plain-language updates, surfacing key milestones, project status, and anticipated handover dates, eliminating the call queues that erode trust. The Post-Sale Service Dispatcher gives homeowners an interface to raise maintenance and Defect Liability Period (DLP)-related service requests; it automatically categorizes issues, routes them to the right technician, prioritizes urgency, and books appointments end-to-end through the same backend workflows already running on Salesforce. For properties with expired DLP coverage, it automatically redirects customers to Inspire Home packages. Both agents operate autonomously, anticipating follow-on service needs before a homeowner raises them.

New Agentic era

“The Mena region is architecting the next Agentic era with real estate at its centre. What Globant built with Aldar is reflection of that ambition: turning years of dormant customer data into an always-on service layer that works without anyone having to ask it to. This is what enterprise AI looks like when it’s done at the scale this region demands,” said Federico Pienovi, CEO of Mena & APAC at Globant.

Aldar Properties, with $9.2 billion in annual revenue and one of the most ambitious development portfolios in the Gulf, faced a challenge familiar across the region: data-rich but insight-poor.

Years of customer interactions, service histories, and property records sat siloed, unable to power real-time decisions. Buyers lacked visibility into construction progress and flooded service teams with low-value queries.

Unified customer layer

Maintenance requests arrived as unstructured text, demanding manual interpretation before any action could be taken. Valuable customer intelligence sat dormant, unable to deliver value before a homeowner even thought to ask for it. Globant's solution rewired that model entirely: activating dormant intelligence through Salesforce Data 360 to create a unified customer layer the agents query autonomously. The result is an improved customer experience: faster access to accurate information, reduced dependency on manual support interactions, and greater transparency throughout the homeowner journey, from construction to post-handover care.

"Our homeowners expect the same intelligence from their property that they experience in every other part of their digital lives. Partnering with Globant has allowed us to deliver real answers, in real time, at any hour. This is the standard Aldar is committed to setting across the region," commented Harry Nakichband, Chief Digital Officer at Aldar Properties.

The solution builds on Globant's 21+ years as a Salesforce partner, with more than 1,200 projects delivered. Globant counts more than 500 Agentforce Certified Specialists and 200+ Salesforce Data 360 specialists. This expertise has earned Globant recognition from Salesforce as an Implementation Level Expert for Data 360, MuleSoft, and Agentforce, the highest distinction a Salesforce Solution partner can earn. This was essential to engineering an agentic architecture that activates years of untapped customer intelligence and scales with Aldar's continued expansion across the Mena region.

The announcement also comes on the heels of Globant being named Salesforce's New Logo of the Year for the second consecutive year at the Salesforce Partner Summit in Dubai. The award recognises Globant's expertise in helping organisations accelerate AI-powered business transformation on the Salesforce Platform.—TradeArabia News Service

data.title: India's August soyoil, palm oil imports rise on stocking
data.description:
By Rajendra Jadhav and Pablo Sinha

India's soyoil imports surged to a record in August, while palm oil purchases climbed to a six-month high, as refiners stocked up ahead of the country's festival season, a leading industry body said on Tuesday.

Higher palm oil and soyoil buying by the world's biggest importer of vegetable oils could help top producers Indonesia, Malaysia and Argentina move their stocks, supporting benchmark palm oil (FCPOc3) and soyoil futures .

India's palm oil imports in August rose 7% from the previous month to 782,761 metric tons, the highest since February, the Solvent Extractors' Association of India (SEA) said in a statement.

Imports of soyoil rose 26% to a record high of 628,736 tons and sunflower oil imports decreased 36% to 160,639 tons, the industry body said.

Overall edible oil imports rose 1.5% to an 11-month high of 1.57 million tons, driven by higher shipments of palm oil and soyoil.

Refiners increased purchases to build stocks ahead of the upcoming festival season, said a Mumbai-based dealer with a global trade house. India celebrates a series of festivals between August and November, when demand for edible oils typically peaks.

Soyoil is available at competitive prices compared with palm oil, which should keep September shipments elevated at above 600,000 tons, said a New Delhi-based dealer with a global trade house.

"Sunflower oil shipments from the Black Sea region have been disrupted by the war. This is also prompting refiners to increase their soyoil purchases," he said.

India's aggressive vegetable-oil buying has led to congestion at major ports, delaying vessel unloading by as much as 10 days as shore tanks fill and refiners struggle to clear incoming cargo, industry officials told Reuters last week.

India sources most of its palm oil ​from Indonesia and ​Malaysia, while ⁠soyoil and sunflower oil are imported mainly from Argentina, Brazil, Russia and Ukraine.

data.title: Uno Minda Approves Rs 1,415 Cr Investment For Capacity Expansion
data.description:
Projects include new aluminium casting and alloy wheel facilities, a Bengaluru moulding expansion and a Maharashtra plant with Toyoda Gosei

Auto components manufacturer Uno Minda on Tuesday announced a series of capacity expansion and plant consolidation projects across its key business verticals, involving a combined investment of around Rs 1,415 crore.

The projects include a new aluminium casting facility in Hosur, a two-wheeler alloy wheel plant in Kharkhoda, expansion of a moulding facility in Bengaluru and a new plant in Maharashtra through its joint venture with Toyoda Gosei, Japan.

Uno Minda said the investments are aimed at increasing manufacturing capacity and meeting demand from original equipment manufacturers (OEMs).

The company will invest Rs 510 crore to establish a greenfield aluminium casting facility at Hosur, Tamil Nadu. The facility will manufacture casting parts for two-wheelers, four-wheelers and commercial vehicles, covering both internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) applications.

The new facility will be developed on an existing land parcel at Thally Road, Hosur, as the company’s current facility at the location has reached its practical expansion limits. The project will increase aluminium casting capacity at Hosur from around 13,000 MT to 34,000 MT at peak capacity.

The expansion will be implemented in phases over the next three years, with the first phase expected to commence production by Q4FY28.

The company’s board has also approved a 3.3 million-unit two-wheeler alloy wheel plant at Kharkhoda, Haryana. The project involves relocating two million units of existing capacity from Supa, Maharashtra, to Kharkhoda and an additional investment of Rs 155 crore. The first phase is expected to commence production by Q4FY28, with the project to be implemented over two years.

Uno Minda’s board has further approved an expansion of its moulding facility in Bengaluru, operated through subsidiary Uno Minda Kyoraku. The expansion, involving an estimated capex of Rs 80 crore, is expected to commence operations by Q1FY28.

Separately, Toyoda Gosei South India, the company’s joint venture with Toyoda Gosei, Japan, will establish a new plant at CSN, Maharashtra, with an estimated investment of Rs 670 crore. The facility will manufacture interior and exterior automotive parts, airbags, hoses and body sealing parts.

The Maharashtra facility will be Toyoda Gosei South India’s third plant in India, following facilities at Bidadi and Harohalli in Karnataka. The project is backed by new customer orders and is expected to commence operations by Q4FY29.

data.title: Epigamia Ropes In Mansi Modi As Marketing Head
data.description:
Modi has over 14 years of experience and has held various leadership roles, including at Hindustan Unilever, Airtel & Britannia

Epigamia has appointed Mansi Modi to lead its marketing. She will step into her new role at the end of September. With that, Rahul Bhagat will lead manufacturing for the company. The new appointments are made on the back of strong business momentum, with the company eyeing an annualised revenue run rate of over Rs 1,000 crore in the next FY, with plans to double its business in the next 24-30 months.

On the news, Ritesh Gauba, CEO, Epigamia says, “We are confident that with Mansi and Rahul joining in, their leadership will help us solidify our growth momentum and strengthen our market leadership. Our strong growth and fundamentals are a testament to our focus on our core innovative products & brand strength. With Mansi and Rahul joining our leadership team, we want to expand into newer formats and keep focusing on our DNA of innovation.”

Modi has over 14 years of experience leading marketing and brand for several organisations in the consumer space. She has held various leadership roles, including at Hindustan Unilever, leading marketing for Oziva, and has previously worked with Airtel & Britannia.

Bhagat brings strong operational excellence in manufacturing, having managed several manufacturing roles in organisations like Danone, Britannia, ITC Foods, Tata Consumer, etc. He will play a pivotal role in strengthening the organisation’s manufacturing capabilities as the company expands rapidly across the country.

The company also reported that Ankur Goel, COO, will be moving on from the business after a decade of startup life, for personal reasons to focus on health & family.

data.title: Bhel Board Approves Rs 65 Cr Investment In NTPC JV
data.description:
Further equity contribution will be made in one or more tranches while Bhel maintains its 50 per cent stake in NBPPL

State-owned engineering company Bharat Heavy Electricals (Bhel) said on Monday that its board has approved a further equity investment of Rs 65 crore in NTPC Bhel Power Projects (NBPPL), its joint venture with NTPC.

The investment will be made by Bhel in one or more tranches as its equity contribution to NBPPL, according to an exchange filing.

Bhel and NTPC hold 50 per cent each in NBPPL. The additional equity investment will be made at face value by both promoter companies and on an arm’s-length basis. Bhel said its 50 per cent shareholding in the joint venture will be maintained.

Joint Venture Operations

NBPPL was incorporated in April 2008 to execute engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contracts for power plants and other infrastructure projects, besides manufacturing and supplying equipment in India and overseas.

The joint venture’s turnover stood at Rs 1.04 crore on a provisional basis in financial year 2025-26, compared with Rs 3.48 crore in 2024-25 and Rs 18.19 crore in 2023-24.

The board approved the investment at its meeting held on 14 September 2026.

data.title: PNC Infratech Stock Falls 20% After 3 Yr NHAI, MoRTH Bidding Ban
data.description:
As of June, NHAI-related projects account for around 36 per cent of the company’s order book of approximately Rs 19,200 crore

Shares of PNC Infratech fell 20 per cent to hit the lower circuit on Tuesday after the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) extended a three-year debarment to the infrastructure company, barring it from bidding for new projects of NHAI, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and their executing agencies.

The action follows structural distress reported on a stretch of the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway Package-II, where PNC Infratech’s subsidiary Awadh Expressway is the concessionaire. NHAI had initiated show-cause proceedings last month over the issue.

The latest development is significant for PNC Infratech because of its dependence on government highway projects. As of June, NHAI-related projects accounted for around 36 per cent of the company’s order book of approximately Rs 19,200 crore.

However, the debarment does not affect the execution of ongoing projects or projects for which PNC Infratech has already emerged as the lowest bidder. The company said it is evaluating legal remedies against the order.

The dispute relates to the six-lane, upgradable-to-eight-lane Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway Package-II in Uttar Pradesh, which was awarded under the Hybrid Annuity Model at a bid project cost of Rs 1,513 crore.

Certain stretches of the project were affected following heavy and continuous rainfall. PNC Infratech had earlier said the affected portion was around 300 metres, representing less than 0.5 per cent of the total expressway length, with most of the affected sections subsequently repaired.

NHAI had proposed several measures in August, including a penalty equivalent to 2 per cent of the performance security, possible debarment of certain technical personnel for up to three years and a downgrade of the concessionaire’s pavement condition rating.

The company had maintained at the time that it had neither been debarred nor declared a non-performer and that it remained eligible to bid for new projects. The latest NHAI action changes that position.

The three-year restriction creates uncertainty around PNC Infratech’s ability to replenish its order book through new NHAI and MoRTH contracts, even though existing execution remains unaffected.

The impact is particularly relevant given the company’s exposure to NHAI-related work. While the current order book provides visibility for ongoing execution, the inability to participate in fresh bids could weigh on future order inflows if the restriction remains in place.

PNC Infratech has also faced regulatory action in the past. In October 2025, the company was subjected to a one-year bidding ban following bribery-related allegations, which was subsequently reduced to four months.

Following Tuesday’s decline, the stock was locked at Rs 140.32, around 57 per cent below its 52-week high of Rs 325.15. The stock has fallen around 45 per cent so far in 2026. The 20 per cent decline is its sharpest single-day fall since October 21, 2024, when it also fell 20 per cent.

This version makes the NHAI exposure and future order-flow risk the core of the story, with the stock movement used as the market reaction rather than the main narrative.

data.title: Fintech AI Monetisation Likely Only From FY28: Report
data.description:
AI dominated the Global Fintech Fest 2026, but fintech companies are still focused on operational gains as monetisation remains at an early stage

India’s fintech industry is rapidly developing artificial intelligence (AI)-based products across payments, lending, customer service and merchant operations, but meaningful revenue from these capabilities is likely to emerge only from FY28 onwards, according to Emkay Research.

In a report following the Global Fintech Fest 2026, the brokerage said AI was the dominant theme at the event, with 144 of 452 sessions, or 32 per cent, explicitly focused on AI or agentic AI. However, adoption and monetisation remain at an early stage, with none of the companies covered by the report disclosing revenue from their new AI products.

Emkay expects the initial benefits of AI to come largely through operational improvements, including lower service costs, better customer support and faster technology integration. The brokerage said the extent to which these gains translate into higher usage and revenue should become clearer over the near to medium term.

AI Moves Across Fintech

The report identified four broad areas where fintech companies are deploying AI: products for banks and other financial institutions, consumer and merchant applications, internal operations, and agentic payments that can execute transactions with limited or no human involvement.

Products showcased at the fest reflected this wider adoption. Paytm demonstrated an AI platform for banks, lenders, insurers and small merchants, with tools spanning customer service, sales, fraud assessment and marketing, while PhonePe showcased AI-based search, transaction insights and merchant tools.

Eternal presented its conversational AI platform for sales, customer support, recovery and onboarding. Razorpay showcased an AI account manager for small businesses and a proprietary payments model trained on roughly 3 trillion data points across 4 billion payments.

Pine Labs also showcased technology that enables AI agents to make purchases when preset conditions are met, while exploring potential revenue generation from UPI transactions. These launches, however, have yet to translate into disclosed AI-specific revenue for the companies covered by the report.

Agentic Payments Face Hurdles

The development of agentic payments could open another area for fintech monetisation, but regulation remains a constraint. Emkay noted that the Unified Agent Protocol for small autonomous debits was still pending at the close of the fest, while human checkpoints remain necessary for such transactions.

The broader digital infrastructure supporting fintech is already operating at significant scale. UPI recorded 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore in August 2026, while the Unified Lending Interface had more than 64 lenders and 136 data services.

Emkay said fintech product launches should be viewed as a “leading indicator of ambition rather than of earnings”. Proprietary data and distribution are likely to determine which AI capabilities eventually translate into meaningful business growth, the brokerage said.

The report therefore expects AI-led revenue to remain a FY28 and beyond story, even as companies continue expanding their AI offerings. For now, the more immediate impact is likely to come from efficiency gains and improvements in servicing and insights rather than a significant new revenue stream.

data.title: Indian IT Stocks Rally As AI Leaders Call For Slower Development; Nifty IT Up 5%
data.description:
Infosys, TCS and HCLTech together add more than Rs 85,000 crore in market capitalisation

Indian IT stocks surged on Tuesday as investors reassessed the near-term threat posed by artificial intelligence to traditional software and outsourcing businesses after senior AI executives called for a more measured pace of development.

The Nifty IT index gained nearly 5 per cent in early trade, with Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and HCLTech among the biggest contributors. The three companies together added more than Rs 85,000 crore in market capitalisation in the first few minutes of trading, while the combined market-cap gain across Nifty IT constituents approached Rs 1.2 lakh crore.

The rally followed a sharp rebound in US-listed Indian IT stocks on Monday. Infosys and Wipro’s American depositary receipts gained 4.8 per cent and 5.5 per cent, respectively, while US technology services companies including Cognizant, Accenture and ServiceNow also advanced.

The change in sentiment follows Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s call for AI companies to slow the pace at which they develop increasingly capable models. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and xAI’s Elon Musk have also backed a more cautious approach.

Amodei has stressed that the proposal does not call for an end to AI development or model training. Instead, he wants companies to use the additional time to strengthen safeguards and allow independent evaluators to assess the safety of increasingly capable systems.

For Indian IT companies, the debate offers a potential reprieve after investors spent much of the past two years pricing in rapid AI-led disruption to traditional software development, maintenance and outsourcing businesses. The Nifty IT index remains about 37 per cent below its record high, according to Bloomberg data.

The latest rally does not eliminate the longer-term uncertainty surrounding AI’s impact on the sector. Indian technology services companies remain exposed to changes in demand for traditional coding and outsourcing work as AI models become more capable.

A gauge tracking TCS and Infosys has lost around USD 226 billion in market value from its December 2024 peak, reflecting investor concerns over the potential impact of generative AI on their business models.

The sector’s valuations have also fallen sharply. The Nifty IT index trades at around 16 times forward earnings, roughly two standard deviations below its five-year average, according to Bloomberg data. Several major IT stocks remain down between 20 per cent and 35 per cent so far this year despite Tuesday’s rebound.

The prospect of slower AI development could therefore provide near-term relief by extending the timeline for disruption, but investors are likely to focus increasingly on whether the sector can translate that additional time into stronger growth and adapt its business models to AI.

data.title: Manish Kothari To Exit Kotak Mahindra Bank After 31 Years
data.description:
Group President and Head of Commercial Banking will step down on 30 September as the lender integrates commercial banking into its retail and institutional segments

Kotak Mahindra Bank Group President and Head of Commercial Banking Manish Kothari will step down from the lender on 30 September 2026, ending a 31-year association with the Kotak Group. Kothari submitted his resignation on 10 September and will leave at the close of business on 30 September.

Veteran Executive Steps Down

Kothari has spent more than three decades with the organisation, including over 15 years in its core leadership team. According to the bank, he plans to pursue opportunities outside Kotak, including the possibility of launching an entrepreneurial venture.

In his resignation letter, Kothari said he had discussed his future plans with Managing Director and CEO Ashok Vaswani several months ago. He also said he had worked with the bank’s whole-time directors and business leaders to facilitate a smooth transfer of responsibilities.

Commercial Banking Structure Changes

Kothari’s departure comes as Kotak Mahindra Bank reorganises its commercial banking operations. The lender will no longer operate commercial banking as a standalone business under a separate head.

Instead, the portfolio will be integrated into the bank’s existing retail and institutional segments. The transition process has already commenced.

Kothari has led the commercial banking business since 2022, overseeing areas including agri finance, rural finance, logistics finance, infrastructure finance, microcredit and gold loans.

Leadership Changes Continue

The exit comes amid wider leadership changes at Kotak Mahindra Bank. Earlier, Vaswani indicated that he would not seek reappointment after completing his current term on 31 December 2026.

Kothari’s departure marks another significant leadership transition for the lender as it prepares for changes to its senior management structure.

Focus On Business Integration

With commercial banking set to be absorbed into the broader retail and institutional segments, the bank’s focus will now shift to executing the integration while maintaining continuity across its lending and financing businesses.

Kothari’s exit also marks the departure of one of the Kotak Group’s longest-serving senior executives after more than three decades with the organisation.

data.title: HFCL Raises Planned Capex To Rs 1,800 Cr For Capacity Expansion
data.description:
Expansion will add 46 lakh fibre Kms of optical fibre, 56.4 lakh fibre Kms of cable and 300 MT of preform capacity

Telecom gear maker HFCL has increased its planned capital expenditure to Rs 1,800 crore to expand manufacturing capacity for optical fibre, optical fibre cable and preform, according to a company filing on Monday.

The company’s board has approved additional capacity of 46 lakh fibre kilometres (Kms) per annum for optical fibre, 56.4 lakh fibre Kms per annum for optical fibre cable and 300 metric tonnes (MT) per annum for preform, which is used to manufacture optical fibre.

The additional capital expenditure for the proposed expansion is estimated at around Rs 820 crore, HFCL said. The investment will be funded through a mix of internal accruals, proceeds from the preferential issue of warrants already issued to the promoter and promoter group entity, and borrowings from financial institutions, among other sources.

The latest expansion is in addition to Rs 980 crore in capital expenditure already approved by the board. This takes the total planned capital expenditure for the capacity expansion initiatives to approximately Rs 1,800 crore.

Upon completion of the planned expansions, HFCL’s manufacturing capacity for optical fibre is expected to increase to 43.1 million fibre Kms per annum, while optical fibre cable capacity is expected to reach 62 million fibre Kms per annum.

The company’s preform manufacturing capacity is expected to increase to 600 MT per annum following completion of the capacity expansions.

data.title: PNC Infratech Faces 3-Year NHAI Bid Ban Over Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway Damage
data.description:
NHAI extends debarment of PNC Infratech’s concessionaire Awadh Expressway to parent company following damage to a stretch of the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway

PNC Infratech has been barred from participating in bids floated by the National Highways Authority of India, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and their executing agencies for three years following damage to a section of the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway.

The action comes after NHAI extended the debarment of PNC Infratech’s subsidiary and concessionaire, Awadh Expressway Private Ltd, to the parent company in its capacity as promoter. PNC Infratech said it received the communication from NHAI on 11 September and that both the company and Awadh Expressway are evaluating legal remedies.

Damage To Expressway Stretch Triggers Action

The matter relates to damage to an isolated stretch of the six-lane Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway. PNC Infratech had earlier said heavy and continuous rainfall had affected around 300 metres of the expressway, representing less than 0.5 per cent of its total length.

The affected project, Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway Package-2, has a bid project cost of Rs 1,513 crore. It had received both provisional and final completion certificates and was in the maintenance phase when the damage occurred. PNC had said most of the affected stretches had subsequently been repaired, with work continuing on the remaining portions.

NHAI Had Earlier Issued Show-Cause Notices

The latest debarment follows show-cause notices issued by NHAI to Awadh Expressway over the damage. The earlier proceedings included a proposed penalty equivalent to 2 per cent of the performance security, debarment proceedings against certain technical personnel for up to three years and a proposed downgrade of the concessionaire's Pavement Condition Index rating.

PNC Infratech had previously maintained that it had not been debarred or declared a non-performer by NHAI at that stage and said it was responding to the notices.

The company had also said repair costs were covered under its routine maintenance obligations and that there was no material impact on its financial position, ongoing projects or eligibility to bid for new projects at the time.

Three-Year Restriction Hits New Road Bids

With the latest NHAI communication, the restriction now directly extends to PNC Infratech, preventing it from participating in bids floated by NHAI, MoRTH and their executing agencies for three years.

The company said the order would not affect its status as a going concern or the execution, operation and maintenance of its ongoing projects. It added that it would disclose any financial implications once greater clarity emerges.

The development has also weighed on investor sentiment, with PNC Infratech shares falling sharply in Tuesday's trading session following the NHAI action.

data.title: Air India Faces Show-Cause Notice Over Delhi Immigration Lapse
data.description:
Civil Aviation Ministry seeks explanation after three Italian passengers flew from Delhi to Munich without completing mandatory immigration formalities

The Ministry of Civil Aviation has issued a show-cause notice to Air India over an alleged procedural lapse at Delhi airport that allowed three Italian passengers to board a connecting international flight without completing mandatory immigration formalities. The passengers had travelled from Amritsar to Delhi on an Air India flight before boarding a Lufthansa service to Munich on 4 September.

The incident has raised concerns over passenger-handling and immigration protocols at Indira Gandhi International Airport, particularly the coordination required when passengers transfer from domestic to international services. The ministry has sought an explanation from Air India CEO and Managing Director Campbell Wilson over the lapse.

Passengers Bypassed Mandatory Immigration

According to sources cited in the report, the three passengers were issued boarding passes at Amritsar for both their Air India flight to Delhi and the onward Lufthansa flight to Munich.

However, their itinerary did not fall under Air India's applicable hub-and-spoke arrangement. Under the arrangement, passengers travelling from designated airports can complete immigration formalities at the originating airport before connecting to an international flight at a hub.

In this case, the passengers were required to exit through the arrival area after reaching Delhi and complete immigration before proceeding to their international departure. Instead, they were directed to the international transfer area, enabling them to bypass the immigration counter before boarding the Munich-bound flight.

Air India-Lufthansa Interline Arrangement Under Scrutiny

The passengers were travelling on a connecting itinerary involving Air India and Lufthansa. The two airlines have an interline partnership, under which passengers can book connecting flights operated by different carriers under a single itinerary.

The incident has brought renewed focus on how such connecting passengers are processed when an itinerary does not qualify for domestic-to-international transfer under the airline's hub-and-spoke procedures.

Air India has not commented on the incident so far.

Senior Officials To Review Incident

A meeting to discuss the incident is expected to be chaired by Home Secretary Govind Mohan. Officials expected to participate include senior representatives from the Civil Aviation Ministry, the Intelligence Bureau, the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Bureau of Immigration, Air India and Delhi airport.

The review is likely to examine how the passengers were routed through the airport and whether existing checks and coordination mechanisms were followed. The incident has also prompted scrutiny of the procedures governing passenger transfers between domestic and international flights at major aviation hubs.

data.title: AI-led digital tech stock Kelton Tech Solutions around 7% | Do you own?
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 15 -- AI-led digital tech stock Kellton Tech Solutions rose around 7% in intra-day deals on Tuesday, 15 September, after the firm was chosen to build an enterprise loan integration platform for a leading automotive finance company.

The stock climbed as much as 6.75% to Rs.14.69 per share on the BSE after opening at Rs.13.92. It had closed at Rs.13.76 on Friday, while the Indian stock markets remained shut on Monday on account of Ganesh Chaturthi.

Meanwhile, Indian equities remained under pressure today as elevated crude oil prices, weak global sentiment and concerns over global bond yields ahead of this week's Federal Reserve meeting weighed on the broader market.

According to the company's press release, the platform will serve as an integration foundation for the lender, connecting its origination, customer management, credit assessment and servicing systems with external verification and financial data providers through a single governed layer.

The system will support applicant verification, credit assessment, eligibility decisioning and customer-record synchronisation, while reducing integration complexity across the lending ecosystem.

Kellton said the platform has been designed as a reusable framework, rather than a fixed set of connections. This would allow the automotive finance company to add new providers, channels and product lines onto the same foundation as its business expands. The platform is also designed with security, auditability and transaction integrity requirements for a regulated environment.

The engagement is expected to strengthen Kellton's credentials in financial services, lending technology, enterprise integration, platform engineering and AI-ready modernisation. The company said the governed flow of data created by the platform would also provide a foundation for automation and AI-led decision-making.

Karanjit Singh, CEO APAC, Kellton, said the engagement reflected the company's ability to address complex integration challenges by combining its platform engineering and financial services expertise.

"As financial services move from digitisation towards more connected and intelligent ecosystems, the ability to integrate systems, data and partners seamlessly is becoming increasingly critical. This engagement reflects the kind of complex integration challenges we are well equipped to address, bringing together our platform engineering and financial services expertise to build a scalable, governed foundation that can evolve with the business. Getting this foundation right is also critical to creating the trusted flow of data needed to advance automation, analytics, and AI-led decisioning over time," Singh noted.

Kellton describes itself as an AI-led digital transformation and technology consulting company with global delivery capabilities.

Despite the latest rebound, Kellton Tech Solutions remains significantly below its recent peak. The small-cap stock is currently 47% below its 52-week high of Rs.27.83, recorded on the BSE. At the other end, it touched a 52-week low of Rs.13.10 in March 2026.

It has gained 3.5% in the last 1 month, but declined 8% in 3 months, 16% in 6 months and 47% over the past 1 year.

data.title: Ingram Micro Sets Mid-Term Financial Outlook
data.description:
By Connor Hart

Ingram Micro said it is entering a new chapter, transitioning from a technology distribution company to create an intelligent operating system for the business-to-business, information-technology ecosystem.

"We are uniquely positioned to help connect demand and supply in smarter ways so customers and vendor partners can operate more efficiently and unlock new opportunities for growth," Chief Executive Paul Bay said Tuesday.

At its inaugural Capital Markets Day, Ingram said it expects net sales to grow at a compounded annual rate of 4% to 6% between 2026 and 2029. Gross profit is projected to grow at a compounded annual rate of 5% to 7% over the same period.

In the short term, the company said third-quarter earnings are anticipated to come in at the high end of its previously issued outlook. In July, Ingram had guided for adjusted earnings of 72 cents to 82 cents a share on net sales of $13.55 billion to $13.95 billion.

Analysts polled by FactSet are looking for adjusted earnings of 78 cents a share on sales of $13.79 billion.

data.title: Genworth Issues Statement on Court of Appeal Ruling Against AXA in UK Payment Protection Insurance Case
data.description:
Genworth Financial, Inc. (NYSE: GNW) today issued a statement in response to a UK Court of Appeal ruling against AXA in their case against Santander companies related to liabilities associated with the historic mis-selling of Payment Protection Insurance (PPI) policies. The judgment granted Santander’s appeal resulting in the setting aside of the trial court’s judgment in AXA’s favor for a majority of the indemnity claim. The Court of Appeal also denied AXA’s appeal of the trial court’s judgment rejecting AXA’s contribution claim. In summary, the Court of Appeal judgment results in a finding of Santander being not liable for the vast majority of AXA’s losses resulting from Santander’s mis-selling.

“While we are very disappointed in the decision from the Court of Appeal, we are analyzing the judgment and working with AXA to evaluate next steps, including options for further appeals,” said Tom McInerney, Genworth President & CEO. “Since we have not factored any recoveries from the case into our capital allocation plans, we remain focused on our three strategic priorities: creating shareholder value through Enact, driving growth through CareScout, and maintaining self-sustainability in our Closed Block.”

At issue were losses incurred from mis-selling complaints for PPI underwritten by two companies that AXA acquired from Genworth in 2015. The policies were sold by a company acquired by Santander in 2009.
